citations.quote:
Use smooth fields on Minkowski coordinate space with $x^0=ct$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Components of $x$ are measured in metres. Fix the Dirac matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], so $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$ and $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta$.

For the SI-normalization bookkeeping, let $c>0$ (m s$^{-1}$), $\hbar>0$ (J s), $\mu_0>0$ (N A$^{-2}$), a real charge parameter $q$ (C), and a mass parameter $m>0$ (kg) be symbolic inputs; put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. In the current SI, $c$ and $h$ are defining constants while $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined; the formula below keeps $\mu_0$ symbolic and assigns it no numerical value. Use the lower-potential convention
$$A_a=(-\phi/c,\mathbf A),\qquad F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,$$
where $A_a$ has units T m, $\phi$ is in volts, and $\mathbf A$ is in T m. Define
$$S_0=\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c},\qquad a_a=A_a/S_0,\qquad f_{ab}=\partial_aa_b-\partial_ba_a,$$
$$\mu=mc/\hbar,\qquad g=q\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}=q/\sqrt{\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a.$$
Thus $a_a$ and $\mu$ have units m$^{-1}$, $f_{ab}$ has units m$^{-2}$, and $g$ is dimensionless. For $\psi$ with units m$^{-3/2}$, both $-\tfrac14 f_{ab}f^{ab}$ and $\bar\psi(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi$ have units m$^{-4}$; their integral over $d^4x$ is dimensionless and represents the action divided by $\hbar$ in this normalization.

For a real smooth gauge parameter $\chi$ in webers, put $\alpha=\chi/S_0$ (dimensionless) and use
$$A'_a=A_a+\partial_a\chi,\qquad a'_a=a_a+\partial_a\alpha,\qquad \psi'=e^{ig\alpha}\psi.$$
The induced covariant derivative is $D'_a=\partial_a-ig a'_a$. These are formal mathematical conventions for the later conditional deductions. They do not adopt a measured value of $\mu_0$, identify $q$ with an electron charge, impose charge quantization, or assert that interacting continuum fields exist.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$
and let $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot x)$, $k\in\mathbb Z^n$, be the coordinate
characters on $\mathbb T^n$
([[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]],
[[def-fourier-coefficients-and-trigonometric-polynomials]]). Then:

1. $(e_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}$ is an orthonormal family in the complex Hilbert
   space $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$;
2. it is an orthonormal basis: its closed linear span is $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$;
3. consequently the Fourier expansion
   $f=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}\widehat f(k)e_k$ and Parseval's identity
   $$\|f\|_2^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}|\widehat f(k)|^2,\qquad \langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}\widehat f(k)\overline{\widehat g(k)}$$
   hold for all $f,g\in L^2(\mathbb T^n)$, in the finite-subset-net sense; and
4. the Fourier coefficient map is a surjective linear isometry of
   $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$ onto $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^n,\mathbb C)$.

No Hilbert tensor-product identification is used anywhere.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Integrating this equation over the periodic box gives $0=L^{-3}\int(-\Delta\phi)\,d^3x=L^{-3}\epsilon_0^{-1}\int\rho\,d^3x$, since each periodic first derivative has equal boundary values on opposite faces. Thus neutrality is necessary. For neutral data, integrating $M$ times by parts in a coordinate with $|k_j|\ge|k|/\sqrt3$ gives $|\widehat\rho_k|\le C_M(1+|k|)^{-M}$ for every integer $M\ge0$; the same bound holds uniformly on compact time intervals when the data depend smoothly on time. Therefore the proposed coefficients for $\phi$ and every differentiated Fourier series are absolutely summable: division by $|2\pi k/L|^2$ costs only two powers and $M$ can be taken arbitrarily large.

Under Countable Choice [A2], apply [F1] after rescaling $x=Ly$: the characters $e^{2\pi i k\cdot x/L}$ form a complete basis for $L^{-3}d^3x$. The coefficient formula then gives $|2\pi k/L|^2\widehat\phi_k=\widehat\rho_k/\epsilon_0$ for $k\ne0$ and the zero mode is zero. Absolute convergence from step 1.2 permits termwise differentiation to every order, so the resulting real smooth periodic $\phi$ solves $-\Delta\phi=\rho/\epsilon_0$. Reality follows from $\widehat\rho_{-k}=\overline{\widehat\rho_k}$.
